name: Rosamund Greaves
source_profile:
Countess Rosamund Greaves, House Greaves 
Rosamund, a relatively young northern noble and daughter of the late Earl Edran Greaves, 
inherited a deeply troubled situation. Her father reluctantly joined the northern rebellion and died 

during the siege of one of Dunmere's principal towns. With the northern armies collapsing, 
Rosamund negotiated the surrender of the remaining Greaves forces and swore fealty to the 
young king. Rather than confiscating the entire earldom, Dedericus IV restored its title to 
Rosamund under a new royal charter. She retains her family's ancestral seat, but her authority 
now explicitly derives from the king's mercy and recognition. Her motivations were partly 
pragmatic. She genuinely opposed prolonging the war, but also knew her family's estates would 
be confiscated if she refused to submit. 
Political tension: Some northern veterans consider her a courageous woman who saved her 
people from destruction. Others whisper that she sold her father's legacy for a title. Meanwhile, 
southern hardliners resent the king for allowing a rebel's daughter to retain an ancient lordship.
